Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
933 PM PST Wed Nov 25 2026

.SYNOPSIS...25/856 PM.

Warming temperatures and dry weather is expected most of the week
due to a predominant offshore flow pattern. Temperatures will 
peak on Thanksgiving and Friday with some gusty northeast winds 
at times, then cooling will begin over the weekend. There is an 
increasing possibility of a large storm system around the middle 
of next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (WED-SAT)...25/853 PM.

***UPDATE***

Offshore flow and sunny skies along with 576 dam hgts brought 3 to
6 degrees of warming to the entire area today. These max temps
were 4 to 8 degrees above normal. Offshore flow continues to
increase and is currently between 5 and 6 mb. A wind advisory was
issued for the Santa Lucia mtns across the Central Coast and other
areas will see gusts just below advisory criteria with some
isolated advisory gusts in the windiest locations.

Forecast in on track with ridging pushing hgts to 588 dam and max
temps aided by the offshore flow reaching into the lower to mid 
80s across most csts and vlys.

Forecast is in good shape and no other updates are planned.

***From Previous Discussion***

Temperatures and offshore pressure gradients are both on the
increase. Gradients will peak on Thanksgiving between -5 and -6 mb
and temperatures will peak Friday in the upper 70s to mid 80s
across coast and valleys. It may be  to add some wind advisory 
coverage tonight and or Thursday morning beyond the Central San 
Gabriel Mountains and Santa Susana Mountains but there's low 
confidence with that so am tabling that for now given the minimal
impacts.

Offshore flow will begin to weaken Friday and turn light onshore 
Saturday which will bring temperatures down 4-8 degrees across 
coast and valleys, but little change across the interior.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...25/153 PM.

Next week will be a very active week of weather, though the only
real impactful storm will be mid week. Book end systems on Sunday
night into Monday morning as well as Friday will be relatively 
mild compared to the Tuesday night and Wednesday storm which has 
the potential to be a 1-3"/3-5" system (coast/mountains). Models 
have been indicating it will be a quick but potent cold front with
maybe 6-8 hours of rain as well a strong and gusty winds. The 
current timing shows most of the rain falling during the overnight
hours into early Wednesday morning, but likely some lingering 
showers through the afternoon. And again snow levels mostly over 
8000 feet, but possibly a few inches down to 7000'. Residents in 
sensitive areas should follow this one closely.

&&

.AVIATION...26/0517Z.

At 0435Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

High confidence in all TAFs xcp KPRB where three is a 30 percent
chc of no low clouds or vis obstuction.

Lgt Turbc and LLWS possible at KBUR, KVNY and KCMA 11Z-17Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Good confidence that any east
wind component remains below 7 kts. N to NE winds around 5 kt are
possible from thru 17Z.

KBUR...High confidence in TAF. Lgt turbc and LLWS possible
11Z-17Z.

&&

.MARINE...25/929 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Expecting Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas with 
areas of SCA level winds to persist through Friday. Then conds 
will be largely below SCA levels Friday night through Monday 
before winds increase Monday night to SCA levels or higher ahead 
of an approaching strong storm system.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Expecting SCA level seas lasting 
through at least Friday. E to NE SCA level winds are expected at
times through Friday morning. Winds increase again Monday night 
to SCA levels or higher ahead of an approaching strong storm 
system.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Winds will generally be below SCA
levels, except for the near shore waters from Point Mugu to Santa
Monica, where offshore SCA level winds are expected into Thursday
night. For Friday through Monday, winds and seas are expected to 
remain below SCA. Winds are expected to increase to SCA levels 
Monday night ahead of an approaching strong storm system.

A large, west long period swell will create hazardous boating
conditions through Thursday for the coastal waters, by creating 
large breaking waves near coastlines and possibly also near harbor
entrances. These waves can capsize small vessels. Follow guidance
from local officials.

&&

.BEACHES...25/932 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will move into the coastal
waters, peaking through Thursday morning. This large swell will 
combine with exceptionally high tides to bring large surf to the 
area as well as moderate to significant coastal flooding.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, as
well as the Ventura County coastline, and far eastern portions of
the southern Santa Barbara County coasts now through Thursday
morning. Elsewhere, the surf and coastal flooding issues are a 
bit less, but still concerning. The morning high tide will be the 
timing of greatest concern for coastal flooding, and low lying 
coastal areas with no protection from the ocean will be more 
vulnerable. Coastal structures are at an increased risk for 
damage. There will be many, strong rip currently nearly 
everywhere, strong long shore currents, a risk of sneaker waves, 
large shore pound, coastal erosion. These conditions will lead to 
an increased risk of drowning and make swimming dangerous.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
